question.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations: $$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} & -\frac{8}{3} \\ -\frac{4}{3} & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}-6{t}^{2}+\frac{41}{3}t-8 \\ 3{t}^{2}-\frac{13}{3}t+5\end{aligned}] $$ The complementary solution to this system is given by $$ {x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R. $$ Then, the general solution of the system is
$x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,\,{t}^{2}+\,\,$ $-1$ $\,\,t+\,\,$ {{field-2}} .
$-1$ {{field-3}} $-2$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}-6{t}^{2}+\frac{41}{3}t-8 \\ 3{t}^{2}-\frac{13}{3}t+5\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is polynomial of degree $2.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also polynomial of degree $2,$ i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}{t}^{2}+{b}_{1}t+{c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}{t}^{2}+{b}_{2}t+{c}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]{t}^{2}+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{c}_{1},{c}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ 2{a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ 2{a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} & -\frac{8}{3} \\ -\frac{4}{3} & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}{t}^{2}+{b}_{1}t+{c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}{t}^{2}+{b}_{2}t+{c}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6{t}^{2}+\frac{41}{3}t-8 \\ 3{t}^{2}-\frac{13}{3}t+5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ 2{a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}(\frac{5{a}_{1}-8{a}_{2}}{3}){t}^{2}+(\frac{5{b}_{1}-8{b}_{2}}{3})t+(\frac{5{c}_{1}-8{c}_{2}}{3}) \\ (\frac{-4{a}_{1}+{a}_{2}}{3}){t}^{2}+(\frac{-4{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}}{3})t+(\frac{-4{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}}{3})\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6{t}^{2}+\frac{41}{3}t-8 \\ 3{t}^{2}-\frac{13}{3}t+5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0{t}^{2}+2{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ 0{t}^{2}+2{a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}(\frac{5{a}_{1}-8{a}_{2}-18}{3}){t}^{2}+(\frac{5{b}_{1}-8{b}_{2}+41}{3})t+(\frac{5{c}_{1}-8{c}_{2}-24}{3}) \\ (\frac{-4{a}_{1}+{a}_{2}+9}{3}){t}^{2}+(\frac{-4{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}-13}{3})t+(\frac{-4{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}+15}{3})\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding coefficients of like powers of $t,$ we get the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5{a}_{1}-8{a}_{2}-18}{3}=0 \\ \frac{-4{a}_{1}+{a}_{2}+9}{3}=0 \\ \frac{5{b}_{1}-8{b}_{2}+41}{3}=2{a}_{1} \\ \frac{-4{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}-13}{3}=2{a}_{2} \\ \frac{5{c}_{1}-8{c}_{2}-24}{3}={b}_{1} \\ \frac{-4{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}+15}{3}={b}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first and second equations, we get

$$
{a}_{1}=2,\,{a}_{2}=-1.
$$

Substituting these into the second and third equations, and solving for ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2},$ we get

$$
{b}_{1}=-1,\,{b}_{2}=3.
$$

Finally, substituting these last two values into the fourth and sixth equations, and solving for ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2},$ we have

$$
{c}_{1}=1,\,{c}_{2}=-2.
$$

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}-t+1 \\ -{t}^{2}+3t-2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{t}^{2}+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
